out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw eggs were stored over noodles and other ready to eat foods in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw fish was stored over ready-to-eat noodles and vegetables in the walk-in. Additionally, raw fish and squid was stored with cooked shrimp in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The PIC corrected all of these issues during inspection.

violations.title: Cover Foods in Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped or uncovered food in the following location where the food is subject to contamination: several food stored in the walk-in refrigerator were uncovered.
violations.corrective_action: Foods shall be protected from contamination by being stored in packages, covered containers or wrappings unless being cooled. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: several containers of kimchi and soup for retail sale packaged in the establishment and stored in the walk-in refrigerator for more than 24 hours were not labeled and were not scheduled to be labeled until tomorrow.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The PIC had a food employee labeled all the containers during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: most of the hot foods in the new hot holding cabinets were date marked improperly. The sell by time was the same time as the prepared time. The PIC thought that since these items were in a holding unit, they no longer required a four hour expiration time however, the hot holding unit was not keeping the foods hot enough, so the foods were still on time as a public health control, not temperature.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. The PIC submitted a work order to have the hot holding units adjusted. The expiration times had not been reached yet, and the PIC changed all the expiration times on the food is in the hot holding cabinets during the inspection.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Bleach was stored on the three compartment sink. Food and cleaning chemicals were stored next to each other on a shelf next to the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. The PIC moved the bleach and chemicals during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: four new hot holding cabinets were installed in the customer self-service area. None of them have thermometers installed.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. Provide thermometers in each unit as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: in utensils were being stored in standing water that was 78°F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The PIC empty the water and had the equipment cleaned and sanitized.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed a large clean pot and a large clean bowl was stored on the floor and under the three compartment sink/hand sink and in a manner that exposed the item (s) to contamination.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: a large pan of cooked fried rice was placed to cool (90ºF) in the walk-in but was covered with foil. A pan of noodles was in the walk-in was cooling (83º) but was covered.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Discontinue covering foods while cooling. The foods were uncovered during the inspection.CDI.
